rationale: Objective-C has TWO dependency declarations and the lane read one. `@import Module;` is a clang module import — a `module_import` node whose only named child is a bare `identifier`, with no <> and no quotes to strip, so the preproc_include branch cannot be widened to cover it. Measured on the router's own 322 admitted files through production parseFile before the branch was written (script/m60/objc-call-shape-probe.ts): preproc_include 904 sites / 322 files -> 902 imports + 902 references; module_import 6 sites / 6 files -> 0 edges. All six corpus sites are `@import AFNetworking;` in the AFNetworking example applications. Both labels are published for the same two reasons as `#import`: `imports` is the kind src/lsp/graph_request.ts filters on to answer "what does this file depend on", and `references` is the kind the shared F5 oracle derives for an include. The module's references row carries its OWN reason code — `clang-module-name-not-resolved`, not `include-target-not-resolved` — because a clang module is not a header path and nothing in this walk knows whether the build defines a module under that name.

fileLevel is load-bearing, not decoration: it is what makes the store put the IMPORTING FILE in source_external instead of the file-scope placeholder, which is how src/lsp/graph_request.ts's usages mode reaches the edge
